title: Age Sets
summary: How generational groups organize responsibility and identity.
body: Age sets are one of the most important organizing structures in Murle society. Boys initiated around the same period are grouped into a shared age set, forming bonds of loyalty and mutual responsibility that last a lifetime.

Each age set carries collective duties, from herding and defense in earlier life stages to advisory and leadership roles as members grow older. Progression through age sets is marked by ceremonies that the whole community recognizes.
This structure creates a clear, community-wide understanding of roles and responsibilities at every stage of life, complementing family and clan ties rather than replacing them.
